problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=6 \\  & 4x-7y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/a80ecf94bbd4f0ea4b7a860e340039ca80bc5ccd0d2a19503cb9dcc571558976.png)
Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/ab29f353f00454b6e8eeb490336e2b33d0b2cf6cd47f4d24ac6c8a8f042af628.png)

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/ee5b759f55931cf4935a0763f22c9eb5deedb04f3e247c295aa2a1da09b121b4.png)

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-10$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-5(-10)=-5 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-55.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-55$ and $y=-10.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -55,-10 \rangle.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 16 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{16}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{13}{16}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
